newsitem.title: PERU: Peru denies it bought Sukhoi-25 jets from Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Peru denies it bought Sukhoi-25 jets from Belarus.

text.p: Peru's Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi denied on Tuesday a military leak that the government has purchased 14 Sukhoi-25 fighter jets from Belarus.
"It is not true. Peru has only bought the MiG planes. It has not bought the Sukhois," Pandolfi told reporters.

The government has confirmed but not detailed the recent acquisition of a squadron of MiG-29 fighter jets, but had until Tuesday refused to comment on claims from high-level air force sources that it also purchased a fleet of Sukhois.
The sources say Peru has bought a total of 18 MiGs, 14 Sukhois and a large arsenal of missiles, rockets, bombs and ammunition to equip the planes.
Official military spokesmen have neither confirmed nor denied the information.
The purchase of the planes has raised fears of a regional arms race, particularly between Peru and neighbouring Ecuador. The countries fought over an undeclared border in 1995.

Quito, which itself bought four Israeli K-Fir combat planes earlier this year, has accused Peru of provoking an arms race, and the U.S. State Department also expressed its disappointment with the Lima government.
The arms affair, combined with last week's controversial arrest of retired army general Rodolfo Robles, has sparked a wave of public concern in Peru over the military's still powerful influence.

The detention of Robles, accused of "insubordination" after he accused a military "death squad" of a recent bomb attack on a regional television station, has angered many and brought a growing campaign for his release.

President Alberto Fujimori joined the wave of criticism over the weekend, saying the arrest was procedurally incorrect and warning the military that he could grant a pardon to Robles if that were not rectified by the Supreme Military Council.
